title: Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Localization in Crowded Scenes
Abstract: Real-time anomaly detection and localization in crowded scenes is a challenging problem due to the high density of people and the complex interactions between them. Then, we construct a graph where each node represents a person and the edges represent their spatial and temporal relationships. We then use a graph neural network to learn the normal behavior patterns of people in the scene. Finally, we use anomaly detection algorithms to identify deviations from these normal patterns. title: Real-Time Anomalous Behavior Detection and Localization in Crowded Scenes

title: Convex Sparse Spectral Clustering: Single-view to Multi-view
Abstract: Convex Sparse Spectral Clustering: Single-view to Multi-view This paper proposes a novel Convex Sparse Spectral Clustering (CSSC) framework for single-view and multi-view data analysis. title: Unsupervised learning of object semantic parts from internal states of CNNs by population encoding
Abstract: Unsupervised learning of object semantic parts from internal states of CNNs by population encoding Object recognition often involves decomposing objects into semantic parts, which provides valuable information for understanding object structure and function. This paper explores an unsupervised approach to learn object semantic parts from the internal states of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) using population encoding. These groups of neurons are then used to construct a population code for each part, which allows us to represent object parts in a compact and meaningful way. Abstract: TransCut: Transparent Object Segmentation from a Light-Field Image This paper presents TransCut, a novel method for segmenting transparent objects from light-field images. title: Fidelity-Naturalness Evaluation of Single Image Super Resolution
Abstract: Fidelity-Naturalness Evaluation of Single Image Super Resolution This paper explores the trade-off between fidelity and naturalness in single image super-resolution (SISR) algorithms. By analyzing the performance of various SISR algorithms on a benchmark dataset, we identify the factors that contribute to the fidelity-naturalness trade-off. Our findings suggest that achieving high fidelity can sometimes come at the expense of naturalness, and vice versa. title: Ground-truth dataset and baseline evaluations for image base-detail separation algorithms
